references.text: Describes the guilt offering (אָשָׁם) and the atonement performed by the priest, the same theme as in Num 5:8 with a guilt offering and atonement.
Refers to the guilt offering with a ram (אֵיל) used for atonement, parallel to the 'ram for atonement' mentioned in Num 5:8.
States that the guilt offering belongs to the priest, just as Num 5:8 says the restitution goes to the priest when there is no kinsman-redeemer.
Refers to the kinsman-redeemer (גֹּאֵל) and his role in redeeming property, relevant for understanding the concept of the kinsman-redeemer in Num 5:8.
Boaz as a kinsman-redeemer (גֹּאֵל) illustrates the institution of the kinsman-redeemer mentioned in Num 5:8.
Describes how something dedicated to the Lord belongs to the priest, parallel to the restitution going to the Lord and the priest in Num 5:8.
